*   This matches the result of rendering two separate polygons with standard back-to-front blending [S1].

The claim states that the evidence supports the result of rendering two separate polygons with standard back-to-front blending. Source [S1] explicitly derives the mathematical result of blending two polygons back-to-front ($C_{d00} = C_{t1} A_{t1} + C_{t0} A_{t0} (1 - A_{t1}) + C_d (1 - A_{t0}) (1 - A_{t1})$) and then demonstrates that a specific register combiner setup produces the exact same final color value ($C_{d00}$) when blended into the frame buffer. The text concludes: 'Using this register combiner setup we obtain exactly the same blending results for multi-texturing as for rendering two separate polygons using single textures.' Thus, the evidence fully supports the claim.
